h: OpenFOAM Case Structure
t: This is the canonical breadth-first map of an OpenFOAM case as OpenFOAM Studio should understand it.

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 1. Three top-level directories
OpenFOAM Case Structure › 1. Three top-level directories › system/
t: Controls the run itself: - controlDict : start/end time, timestep, write behavior, selected solver module - fvSchemes : discretization choices - fvSolution : linear solvers and alg

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 1. Three top-level directories › constant/
t: Holds mesh and physical/model configuration: - polyMesh/ : generated mesh files after meshing - physicalProperties : transport coefficients such as nu - momentumTransport : laminar

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 1. Three top-level directories › 0/
t: Initial conditions and boundary conditions for fields at time zero: - U : velocity - p : pressure - additional fields depend on solver/model selection

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 2. Minimum valid case for the current repo
t: The repo’s current cavity path needs exactly these eight authored files: - 0/U - 0/p - constant/physicalProperties - constant/momentumTransport - system/controlDict - system/fvSche

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 3. Dependency graph
t: The agent should think about file generation in this order: 1. system/controlDict 2. constant/physicalProperties 3. constant/momentumTransport 4. system/blockMeshDict 5. field list

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 4. Boundary consistency rule
t: Every mesh patch must appear in every relevant field file. For the current cavity case: - mesh patches: movingWall , fixedWalls , frontAndBack - 0/U must contain all three - 0/p mu

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 5. 2D convention in OpenFOAM
t: OpenFOAM cases are still built on a 3D mesh structure. A 2D case is usually represented by: - one cell in the thin direction - empty type on the front/back patches - empty boundary

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 6. What changes when the case becomes more complex
OpenFOAM Case Structure › 6. What changes when the case becomes more complex › Turbulent incompressible cases
t: Usually add turbulence fields such as: - k - epsilon - omega - nut

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 6. What changes when the case becomes more complex › Imported or external meshes
t: The authored mesh file may no longer be blockMeshDict . Instead the workflow may require: - mesh conversion utility - manually checked patch typing - edited constant/polyMesh/bound

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 6. What changes when the case becomes more complex › Multiphase or compressible cases
t: Expect more fields, more property dictionaries, and different solver modules.

h: OpenFOAM Case Structure › 7. Agent heuristics
t: - Infer the minimum file set from the solver and model family - Prefer tutorial-derived structures over invention - Treat system/ , constant/ , and 0/ as coupled, not independent -

h: Reviewer Checklist
t: Use this checklist when the solver fails, the mesh fails, or the result looks physically wrong.

h: Reviewer Checklist › 1. First classify the failure
t: Choose one primary class: - file structure error - OpenFOAM syntax error - missing patch / boundary mismatch - wrong solver-module-era naming - mesh validity error - numerical inst

h: Reviewer Checklist › 2. Fast inspection order
t: Inspect in this order: 1. system/controlDict 2. constant/momentumTransport 3. system/blockMeshDict 4. all files in 0/ 5. system/fvSolution 6. system/fvSchemes This order catches mo

h: Reviewer Checklist › 3. Questions to ask on every review
Reviewer Checklist › 3. Questions to ask on every review › Version correctness
t: - Did the case use OpenFOAM 13 names? - Is the runner foamRun ? - Is the solver module set correctly?

h: Reviewer Checklist › 3. Questions to ask on every review › Mesh/field integrity
t: - Do field patch names exactly match mesh patch names? - Are empty patches handled consistently? - Does the mesh describe the intended geometry?

h: Reviewer Checklist › 3. Questions to ask on every review › Physics integrity
t: - Does nu match the requested Reynolds number? - Is laminar vs turbulent choice reasonable? - Are pressure conditions appropriate for a closed domain?

h: Reviewer Checklist › 3. Questions to ask on every review › Numerics
t: - Is deltaT too large? - Are the algorithm blocks compatible with the chosen module? - Did residuals decrease?

h: Reviewer Checklist › 4. Minimal-fix policy
t: The reviewer should prefer the smallest safe correction: - fix one wrong keyword before rewriting a full file - preserve existing patch names if they are mesh-consistent - avoid ch

h: Reviewer Checklist › 5. What the reviewer should never do casually
t: - rename mesh patches after field files already depend on them - switch between modular and legacy solver styles mid-case - add extra turbulence fields without updating all depende

h: Reviewer Checklist › 6. Physical-fidelity review
t: Even if the run succeeds: - compare output against expected qualitative behavior - compare benchmark profiles where available - check that boundary conditions represent the intende

h: Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match
Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match › Boundary mismatch
t: - keyword <patchName is undefined in dictionary

h: Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match › Solver/linear solver mismatch
t: - Unknown asymmetric matrix solver PCG

h: Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match › Pressure reference issue
t: - pressure singularity or no reference point behavior

h: Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match › Instability
t: - rapidly growing residuals - very large Courant number - nan , inf , or floating point failure

h: Reviewer Checklist › 7. Log clues to pattern-match › Mesh issues
t: - negative volume cells - bad non-orthogonality or skewness from checkMesh

h: Reviewer Checklist › 8. Output expected from a reviewer AI
t: A good reviewer response should include: - root cause in one sentence - exact file to change - exact keyword or block to change - why the change is safe - whether the fix is: - syn
